title: Meetings and introductions at work
subtitle: Je vous présente ... — Enchanté(e) !
summary: Introduce colleagues, ask someone's name, organise a meeting and write a short professional email in French.

lesson.heading: Introductions at the office
lesson.text: To introduce someone, say **Je vous présente** + name + job (or **je te présente** to a friend). In a hurry, the name and job alone will do. The answer is always **Enchanté !** - with an extra *-e* in writing when a woman says it.

examples.note: Hello. (I'm) Philippe Le Goff.

examples.text: **Je vous présente** deux de mes collaborateurs : Sébastien Meyer, notre responsable clientèle...
examples.note: Let me introduce two of my colleagues: Sébastien Meyer, our customer relations manager...
Pleased to meet you! (a man / a woman speaking)
Viviane Hulot, my assistant. - Pleased to meet you!

examples.text: Je vous ai déjà parlé au téléphone, je crois.
examples.note: I think I've already spoken to you on the phone.

lesson.heading: Asking someone's name: s'appeler
lesson.text: **S'appeler** is a reflexive verb. Use inversion in polite or written French, and the name at the end in casual speech.

examples.text: **Comment vous appelez-vous ?** / Vous vous appelez comment ? (familiar)
examples.note: What's your name?
My name is Victor Chan.
What's her name? - Her name is Lise.
What's your name? (to a friend)

lesson.heading: Organising a meeting
rows: send the invitations to the meeting
envoyer **une note de service** par mail
lesson.note: Typical documents: **un tableau** (a table / spreadsheet), **un graphique** (a chart), **un contrat**. *Un mail* = *un courriel* (an email).

lesson.heading: Places of work and the company
lesson.text: Each job has its own workplace. A company also has **des concurrents** (competitors, who make or sell the same kind of product) and **des fournisseurs** (suppliers, who sell it the materials it needs).

examples.note: Office workers work in an office.

examples.text: Les ouvriers fabriquent des produits dans **une usine**.
examples.note: Factory workers make products in a factory.

examples.text: Un médecin, un avocat, un notaire travaillent dans **un cabinet**.
examples.note: A doctor, a lawyer, a notary work in a practice.

examples.text: Une vendeuse travaille dans **un magasin** / **une boutique**.
examples.note: A shop assistant works in a shop.

lesson.heading: Bien: checking and confirming
lesson.text: Slip **bien** after the verb to check that something is right (in a question) or to confirm it (in a statement). It is not *well* here, more like *really* or *indeed*.

examples.note: You are the customer relations manager, aren't you?
She does work in Limoges, doesn't she?
He did receive the documents.
I have received your email. (standard email opening)

lesson.heading: Key expressions for work emails
lesson.text: These fixed phrases make an email sound professional. **Tiens !** shows surprise, and **Évidemment !** is a strong *of course!*

examples.text: **N'hésitez pas à me contacter.** / **N'hésitez pas à m'appeler.**
examples.note: Don't hesitate to contact me / to call me.
Thank you in advance.
Best regards. (written)

examples.text: **Tiens**, c'est bizarre, il ne m'a rien dit.
examples.note: Well, that's odd, he didn't tell me anything.
Of course I phoned them!

lesson.text: French companies hold a lot of meetings - some people joke about *la réunionite*, "meeting-itis". People like to discuss and convince before acting, and they prefer to say *Nous sommes arrivés à **un accord*** rather than talk of a *consensus*, which can sound negative.

exercises.prompt: Match each word with what it is.

pairs.right: the list of topics for the meeting
the document written after the meeting
a memo for a whole group of colleagues
companies that sell the same product

context.label: From the dialogue
context.text:
*Sébastien :* Bonjour, madame. Enchanté !
*Colette :* Enchantée ! Je vous ai déjà parlé au téléphone, je crois.

exercises.statement: Colette a déjà parlé à Sébastien.
exercises.explanation: She says she has already spoken to him **au téléphone**.

context.label: From the dialogue
context.text: *Philippe :* ... Et Jean-Paul Becker, notre responsable de la fabrication.

exercises.statement: Jean-Paul est responsable de la clientèle.
exercises.explanation: Jean-Paul is in charge of **la fabrication** (production); Sébastien handles the customers.

context.label: From the dialogue
context.text:
*Solange :* Ils m'ont aussi demandé votre adresse électronique. Je leur ai seulement donné votre adresse professionnelle.
*Philippe :* Vous avez bien fait.

exercises.statement: Solange a donné l'adresse personnelle de Philippe.
exercises.explanation: She gave only his **adresse professionnelle** - his work address.

context.label: From the dialogue
context.text: *Solange :* Patrice m'a demandé de reporter la réunion de mardi à jeudi. Apparemment, certains fournisseurs ne sont pas disponibles, ce jour-là.

exercises.statement: Certaines personnes ne peuvent pas venir à la réunion mardi.
exercises.explanation: Some suppliers are **pas disponibles** on Tuesday, so the meeting is postponed to Thursday.

context.label: From the dialogue
context.text: *Adrienne :* Regarde, j'ai reçu les chiffres du trimestre. Ils sont franchement mauvais.

exercises.prompt: What are the quarter's figures like?
Pendant une réunion, on ___ des notes.
Il est ouvrier, il fabrique des voitures, il travaille dans une ___.
exercises.explanation: Factory workers (*les ouvriers*) work in **une usine**.

exercises.prompt: Elle est avocate, elle travaille dans un ___.
exercises.explanation: Lawyers, doctors and notaries work in **un cabinet**.

exercises.prompt: You want to confirm to a client that you have received their documents. What do you write?
Which of these is NOT a good way to end an email to a new client?
options: Je vous en remercie par avance.
exercises.explanation: *Salut* is for friends. With a client, use **Bien à vous** or **N'hésitez pas à me contacter**.

exercises.prompt: Introduce your assistant: "Let me introduce Viviane Hulot, my assistant."
exercises.answer: Je vous présente Viviane Hulot, mon assistante.
